title: The Slow train to the city
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：slow　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 slow 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the baker wrote of ① a slow train to the city in the bill, and everybody in the bakery said at once that it was ② slower than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the baker, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the slow ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the slowest train to the city anybody in the bakery had ever seen, or so the bill for December 1949 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too slow to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the slow ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tray at the far oven, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a slow reply from the office, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as slow as the reply from the office they had once had in the old bakery. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was slow or not, and he said so.

By 1962 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the bill. What the line asked for was ⑦ something slow, and nothing besides. The customer from the next bakery called the whole plan ⑧ quite slow; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the bill kept the names of the slow ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1965, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another slow train to the city in the same bill, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ slower than anybody had expected. ⑩ The slowest reply from the office in the whole bakery, she said in 1967, was the one she could never quite name; the slow ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 慢（前置定语 a slow train to the city：1955 年面点师在账单里记下的那件慢的车）
B. adj. 慢／迟缓（比较级 slower than：文中两处，一处比开往城里的慢车，一处比预想）
C. adj. 慢／迟缓（最高级 the slowest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 慢（表语 too slow to do：母亲觉得它太慢，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 迟缓（前置定语 a slow reply from the office：叔叔把整件事称作一桩迟缓的答复）
F. adj. 迟缓（同级比较 as slow as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩办公室迟缓的答复相比）
G. adj. 迟缓（后置定语 something slow：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 迟缓（受程度副词修饰 quite slow：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a slow train to the city
the slowest train to the city anybody
a slow reply from the office
The slowest reply from the office in

answers.why: slow 意为“慢”，1955 年面点师在账单里记下的是“一件慢的车”，此处作前置定语 a slow train to the city。
slow 意为“慢”，此处用比较级 slower than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
slow 意为“慢”，账单上 十二月 那行字说它是糕饼铺里最慢的一件，故用最高级 the slowest train to the city。
slow 意为“慢”，母亲认为这件东西“太慢了，谁也用不上”，too slow to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
slow 意为“迟缓”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩迟缓的答复”，此处作前置定语 a slow reply from the office。
slow 意为“迟缓”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩办公室迟缓的答复一样迟缓”，同级比较用 as slow as。
slow 意为“迟缓”，账单上那半行字要的是“迟缓的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something slow。
slow 意为“迟缓”，邻糕饼铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当迟缓”，quite 修饰原级 slow。
slow 意为“迟缓”，1965 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要迟缓”，故用比较级 slower than。
slow 意为“迟缓”，母亲 1967 年说的是“整个糕饼铺里最迟缓的那一桩”，故用最高级 the slowest reply from the office。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1955 年，面点师在账单里记下了一件慢的车。（a slow train to the city）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更慢。（slower than …）
母亲觉得它太慢，谁也用不上。（too slow to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩迟缓的答复。（a slow reply from the office）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩办公室迟缓的答复一样迟缓。（as slow as …）
到了 1962 年，账单上只剩半行字：要的是一件迟缓的东西。（something slow）
answers: In 1955 the baker wrote of a slow train to the city in the bill.
Everybody said it was slower than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too slow to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a slow reply from the office.
He said nobody would call it as slow as the reply from the office they had once had.
By 1962 the bill asked for nothing but something slow.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 slow 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1955 the baker wrote of a slow train to the city in the bill, and nobody forgot it.
It was the slowest train to the city in the bakery, or so the bill says.
My mother thought it too slow to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a slow reply from the office, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next bakery called the plan quite slow, and everybody laughed.
The slow ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
